author: Linnaeus, 1758
status: 겨울철새, 해마다 수만 마리 · 여름에도 드물게 기록(10건 미만)
summary: 주로 바닷가와 하구의 갯벌에서 먹이를 찾는 흔한 겨울철새다. 위로 굽은 부리를 펄에 대고 훑어 갯벌에 붙은 해조류와 갑각류 등을 먹는다. 국내에서는 낙동강, 간월호, 금강 하구, 순천만 등지에서 큰 무리를 지어 겨울을 난다. 유럽에서 동쪽으로 몽골, 중국 동북부에 걸쳐 번식하고, 유럽 남부, 북아프리카, 인도 북부, 중국 동부, 한국, 일본에서 겨울을 난다.

points.en: chestnut band across the breast and back

art.subject: Common Shelduck (Tadorna tadorna), adult male in winter, as seen on Korean estuary mudflats from November to March: head and upper neck blackish with a green gloss; lower neck and most of the body white; a broad chestnut band encircling the upper breast and upper back; a black stripe down the centre of the belly; scapulars black, forming a black stripe along each side of the back; primaries black; green speculum; inner tertials partly chestnut; undertail coverts pale cinnamon-orange. Bill bright red, with a rounded knob at the base that swells towards spring; dark eye; pink legs and feet.
art.pose: walking on a mudflat, sweeping its bill through the mud
art.scene: Korean estuary mudflat in winter at low tide; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view walking on mud: green-glossed black head and upper neck, red upturned bill with a knob at the base, chestnut breast band, white body, black scapular stripe, pink legs
adult female, side view walking: like the male but slightly smaller, with no bill knob, a narrower, duller breast band and some white around the bill base
adult in flight seen from above: white back and wing coverts, black flight feathers, green speculum, chestnut band across the upper back, dark head, head, body and tail in a straight line
art.build: Large, goose-like duck, about 61cm, a little larger than a Mallard and longer-legged, standing and walking upright on open mud. Head rounded, neck medium length. Bill shorter than the head, broad, the culmen dipped in the middle so the tip turns slightly upward. Legs medium length, pink, webbed. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip. Tail short. In flight white wings with black flight feathers and a green speculum; wingbeats rather slow and goose-like.
avoid: Do not paint an orange body or a pale head — that is Ruddy Shelduck (Tadorna ferruginea).
Do not paint a dull yellow, Mallard-like bill; it is bright red and slightly upturned.
Do not paint orange or bright red legs; they are pink.
Do not run the chestnut band up the neck; a white collar separates it from the dark head.
